name: abnormal labour overview
title: Abnormal labour: induce labour that has not begun, augment labour that is too slow by fixing the 4 P's, deliver with forceps or vacuum only when fully dilated with the head engaged and otherwise by cesarean section, offer a trial of labour after cesarean only when every criterion is met while watching for uterine rupture, and treat postpartum hemorrhage by its cause and stage; a panel lists the contraindications to labour

root.title: Labour is not going to plan: which fix, in what order?
lines: reach for them in this order: induce or augment → forceps or vacuum → cesarean section (C/S)
the 4 P's: Power (contractions, pushing) · Passage (bony pelvis) · Passenger (presentation, position, size) · Psyche (support)

groups.title: Labour must START or SPEED UP
lines: has it begun? is it moving?

groups.title: Baby must come OUT: which route?
lines: fully dilated + head engaged → instrument; if not → C/S

head: h
Induction of labour
start labour that has not begun
when: • low risk at 39 weeks (ARRIVE): fewer C/S, less preeclampsia, fewer stillbirths
• prelabour rupture of membranes · abruption · twins
• alloimmunization with fetal anemia · fetal demise
• maternal cardiac, respiratory, renal, blood disease
check: • confirm dates · fetal position · estimated weight · consent
• Bishop score: dilation, effacement, position, station
• > 6 favourable: straight to step 2 · shorter, more vaginal births
• also ↑ success: multiparity, ruptured membranes, lower BMI, taller, smaller baby
do: may start labour on its own

head: h
Labour dystocia
abnormally SLOW labour
the #1 reason cited for C/S
NOT shoulder dystocia: shoulder stuck behind the pubic bone, an EMERGENCY
check: Which of the 4 P's? Fix what you can
do: • breech: external cephalic version, before labour
• pain control as she wishes, not an epidural for all

head: h
Forceps or vacuum
speeds up the 2nd stage
when: • atypical or abnormal fetal heart rate (FHR): #1
• must not strain: heart, brain vessels
do: stop: can't apply, no descent, 20 min
• vacuum: cephalohematoma, SUBGALEAL bleed, jaundice, retinal + brain bleeds, Erb's palsy
• forceps: MORE maternal tears, facial nerve palsy, eye trauma
• forceps: facial cuts 1%, cephalohematoma 1%, brain bleed 0.1%
• subgaleal spreads · cephalohematoma stops at sutures

head: h
Cesarean section
the big four = 70% of C/S
1 dystocia · 2 FHR · 3 previous C/S · 4 breech, transverse
when: • herpes, HIV · twins · cervical cancer · fetal anomalies
check: • low transverse: standard, later labour OK
• classical or T: NO labour ever after
• vertical midline: crash, old scar, obesity, bleeding disorder
do: • bladder injury ~1% · bowel, ureter, nerve, vessel injury

head: h
Trial of labour after C/S (TOLAC)
success = vaginal birth after C/S (VBAC), 60–80%
when: • normal pelvis · no contraindication to labour · she consents
check: • uterine cavity entered, or past rupture
• ↑ prior VBAC or vaginal birth · favourable cervix · spontaneous labour · last C/S for breech · age < 40
• ↓ last C/S for dystocia · induction or augmentation · > 40 weeks · > 4000 g · BMI > 30 · hypertension
do: • atypical or abnormal FHR comes FIRST
• pain, bleeding, hematuria, fetal parts palpable, mother unstable
• ↑ risk: more scars, short interval, induction, macrosomia, dystocia
• shorter stay · less pain, blood loss, VTE, infection
• less previa, accreta, hysterectomy next time

head: h
Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH)
> 500 mL vaginal, > 1000 mL at C/S
or ANY loss making her unstable
early < 24 h · late 24 h to 12 weeks
Canada 5.6 per 100 · 60% have risk factors beforehand
when: • tone: overdistension (twins, polyhydramnios, macrosomia), long or fast labour, long oxytocin, infection, fibroids, previa
• trauma: tears, hematoma, rupture, inversion (excess cord traction)
• thrombin: von Willebrand, DIC, HELLP, fetal demise, amniotic fluid embolism, anticoagulants
check: • ORDER: oxygenate, restore volume, drugs, evaluate, remedy the cause
• bimanual exam, fundal massage, empty the bladder (Foley)
do: • full resuscitation: see HEMORRHAGIC SHOCK chart
• still bleeding: Bakri balloon or packing, compression sutures, artery ligation or embolization, hysterectomy
• treat anemia in pregnancy · uterotonic in the 3rd stage

panels.title: NO labour (→ C/S) if ANY of these
items: placenta previa, vasa previa, cord presentation
prior classical C/S or major uterine surgery

panels.title: Breech + cord prolapse
items: breech: frank, complete, footling · external cephalic version before labour
breech risk: uterine anomaly, pelvic tumour, previa, hydro- or anencephaly, oligo- or polyhydramnios, multiparity, twins, previous breech
cord prolapse: overt, occult, or cord presentation (before rupture) · 0.17–0.4% of births
prolapse risk: transverse or footling, polyhydramnios, preterm, unengaged head, twins, PPROM, male
